footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. From pre-tax income to net income: after income tax and $2.7M of discontinued operations. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose 13.1% to $52.1M in 2025. Net interest income rose 15.8% to $48.0M and noninterest income fell 11.1% to $4.1M; noninterest expense rose 6.4%, and the provision for credit losses was $1.7M, versus $31.4M.
Net income was $1.3M, versus −$6.2M, or $0.07 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 87.5% versus 93.0%. FB Bancorp returned $22.2M through buybacks.
watch: Net interest income depends on interest rates.
sources: FB Bancorp, Inc. Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)
